opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll, which is at or below the full-time maximum (write; admin allowed only for role owners). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a CONTRACTOR with BASIC security training (HR note says full_time — discrepancy). Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR note (authoritative for employment type) states Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin only for role owners). Requested write access to Payroll is at or below that maximum, so the requested level is granted. The Security note's contractor classification conflicts, but employment status is determined by HR, and the requested level is policy-compliant under the authoritative facts.
